topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Effective Use
explanation: Computer systems utilize a memory hierarchy—a tiered structure of storage devices—to optimize the trade-off between access latency, capacity, and cost. This structure places smaller, faster, volatile memory (registers, L1/L2 caches) closer to the CPU core. Effective performance hinges on exploiting the principle of locality of reference (temporal and spatial). Caching strategies dictate the policies for block placement, replacement (e.g., LRU, FIFO), and write propagation (write-through vs. write-back). The primary goal is maximizing the cache hit rate and minimizing the miss penalty, thereby reducing the average memory access time (AMAT).
